claim: The 2027 Flemish entrance examinations are on 2 July (medicine), 3 July (dentistry) and 4 July (veterinary medicine), with registration from 1 March to 17 May 2027 inclusive.
excerpt: De toelatingsexamens van 2027 vinden plaats op vrijdag 2 juli (arts), zaterdag 3 juli (tandarts) en zondag 4 juli (dierenarts). Je kan je inschrijven van 1 maart tot en met 17 mei 2027.
interpretation: The medicine exam falls four days before IB results, so it is sat without knowing diploma grades. The country profile records the rule that makes this workable: the diploma must be held by 30 September of the year of ranking.

attestation.by: the France, Belgium and Luxembourg floor pass
attestation.note: The page renders its content in JavaScript; read in a browser. Dutch original.

claim: Flemish higher education is binary: five universities and thirteen university colleges (universities of applied sciences and arts), which alone award associate degrees and professional bachelor degrees; the schools of arts sit inside the university colleges.
excerpt: The Flemish higher education system is a binary system, consisting of 18 publicly funded higher education institutions: five universities […] and 13 small and medium sized university colleges, also known as universities of applied sciences (and arts). […] An associate degree (90-120 ECTS) is a practice-based programme between secondary education and a professional bachelor's degree.

attestation.by: the France, Belgium and Luxembourg floor pass

claim: There is no central Flemish application system: each institution sets its own procedure and dates, and applications generally open around November-December.
excerpt: Each Flemish higher education institution has its own procedures, opening and closing dates for applications […] In general, applications at Flemish higher education institutions open around November-December.

attestation.by: the France, Belgium and Luxembourg floor pass

claim: Flemish bachelor admission rests on a secondary diploma that gives university access in the country that awarded it, and English at B2 is required for most English-taught programmes.
excerpt: For bachelor's studies in Flemish higher education institutions, admission is granted on the basis of a secondary education diploma that gives access to university studies in the country where the diploma was awarded. […] English at level B2 is required for most bachelor's and master's programmes taught in English.
interpretation: The IB is not named. The rule is about the awarding country, which for an IB Diploma is not obvious; confirm with the institution.

attestation.by: the France, Belgium and Luxembourg floor pass

claim: French-speaking Belgian higher education is delivered in three types of institution: universities, university colleges (hautes écoles) and schools of arts.
excerpt: study programmes are delivered in three different types of higher education institutions: universities, university colleges, and schools of arts
interpretation: The page gives counts for each type; they are not carried here because the reading was a summary rather than a check of the figures.

claim: In French-speaking Belgium you apply online on the chosen institution's own website, ideally between February and 31 March; quota programmes such as medicine are entered only by their own procedure.
excerpt: Fill out an admission request on-line, on the website of your chosen higher education institution. […] we recommend you enrol some time in February and 31 March.
interpretation: A recommendation, not a rule. The binding dates are each institution's.

attestation.by: the France, Belgium and Luxembourg floor pass

claim: An IB diploma issued by the IB in Geneva, from a school recognised by the IB, needs no equivalence to enter higher education in French-speaking Belgium.
excerpt: un baccalauréat délivré par l'Office international du Baccalauréat située à Genève (Attention, l'école doit être reconnue par l'Organisation du baccalauréat international et suivre ses programmes).
interpretation: Listed among the diplomas exempt from the equivalence procedure that other foreign secondary diplomas go through by 15 July. General guidance says a foreign diploma needs equivalence; for a full IB Diploma it does not.
